narrative.overview: Epoch Community is where a conversation becomes signed work without leaving the conversation. The interface is built as an orienteering map: a permanent legend, every ink meaning exactly one thing, and one reserved ink carrying the course from talk to signed work. It is read first by people building in the open without version-control fluency, so it teaches its vocabulary by showing the legend rather than by explaining itself in prose.
keyCharacteristics: A permanent legend replaces explanatory copy; when a reader needs to learn a meaning, the legend gains an entry.
Terrain inks (runnable, rough, open land, marsh) are grounds that say where you are; they never carry text weight.
One reserved control ink carries the conversation-to-signed-work path and focus, and nothing else may wear it.
Light throughout, including the rail: a legend prints on the same paper as its map.
Mono is notation — anchors, signatures, paths, measured values — and never prose.
State is never colour-alone: shape, weight and text carry it too.

rules.name: The Surface Is Product Rule
rules.body: The page background must always expose the design system token, never the browser default.

rules.name: The Copper Rarity Rule
rules.body: Copper is for action and attention only. Do not use it as broad decoration or inactive chrome.

rules.name: The Product Type Rule
rules.body: Do not introduce display fonts or decorative type in Community UI. The work is the product.

rules.name: The Flat Until Useful Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest unless the element is a framed tool or a hoverable workflow target.

dos: Do expose CSS custom properties on `:root` so browser tests and future agents can verify the design system.
Do keep cards at 8px radius or below.
Do use semantic landmarks, skip links, visible focus, and reduced-motion handling.
Do keep repository actions concrete: Browse, View Issues, Review Changes.
Do keep Community visually separate from the hosting control plane while preserving shared product discipline.
Do express channel kind as terrain ground (background tint), never a left side-tab stripe.
donts: Don't ship default browser typography, link lists, or white backgrounds.
Don't use gradient text, decorative glass, side-stripe borders, or hero-metric templates.
Don't add inactive saturated color, purple-blue gradients, dark terminal theming, or beige-only palettes.
Don't create dead controls. If an element looks actionable, it must navigate to a route or section.
Don't hide Community workflows in desktop-only navigation. Mobile users must still reach the workflow rail.
Don't use Inter or Inter Display — Helvetica Neue + platform UI sans only.
